solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Thrash dough

definitions.meaning: to beat or thrash them soundly
a soft mixture of flour and water, like a dough

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses belong to one word: a verb for a beating and a noun for a soft flour mixture used in cooking.

clue.text: Utter pillock initially runs against fast cat

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word pillock is wanted here

parts.note: R is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for runs
on can mean against, as in leaning on a wall
the ounce, or snow leopard, is a swift wild cat

explanation.surface: Someone insults a total idiot who is chasing a speedy cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utter' reads as an adjective ('utter pillock') but is the verb defining the answer. PILLOCK is British slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: To utter a word is to say or articulate it, the core sense of the verb.

clue.text: Opposition to purchase new trainee's classes

indicators.note: making something new out of these letters means reshaping them into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A beginner's lessons start up.
explanation.definitionFit: Sales resistance is a shopper's reluctance to be persuaded into buying, a reluctance to purchase.

clue.text: International currency developed by City University

parts.note: EC is the postcode area for the City of London

explanation.surface: A world currency was devised by a London university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed by' is a link: the City of London's postcode sits beside U. The ECU was the European Currency Unit that came before the euro.
explanation.definitionFit: The ECU was a basket unit of account used across European countries, so a currency spanning nations.

clue.text: Concerning dreams about one being trapped in Clapton?

parts.note: on can mean about, as in a talk on a subject

indicators.note: something trapped in another word is held inside its letters

parts.note: Eric Clapton, the guitarist
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A question about a single item imprisoned inside a guitarist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clapton' stands for his first name, ERIC; the numeral goes between its E and R.
explanation.definitionFit: Oneiric is a formal adjective from the Greek for dream, used of anything relating to dreams.

clue.text: Bear grudge and fool English political disciple

parts.note: to owe someone a grudge is an idiom meaning to bear one
a nit is British slang for a foolish person

explanation.surface: Holding resentment and duping an English follower of a politician.
explanation.walkthrough: An Owenite followed Robert Owen, the Welsh-born early socialist and co-operative pioneer.
explanation.definitionFit: Owen's followers formed a political and social movement, so an Owenite is a disciple of that creed.

clue.text: Self-interest and self-concern, say, not crimes when reviewed

parts.note: e.g. stands for for example, which say means here

indicators.note: reviewing the letters means going over them again in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A self-absorbed person insists they are no criminal once their case is reconsidered.
explanation.definitionFit: Egocentrism is a fixation on oneself, regarding one's own interests and outlook as central.

clue.text: Outrageous Oscar is pretty clever, with hindsight

indicators.note: something outrageous is wild and out of order, telling us to rearrange these letters

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Looking back, a flamboyant Oscar was rather brilliant.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oscar in the surface suggests Wilde, but only gives its phonetic-alphabet letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Retrospectively means looking back on past events, which is judging them in hindsight.

clue.text: Buoyancy aid reached over lake

indicators.note: in a down entry, one part placed over another comes first

parts.note: came means arrived at or reached
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A float drifted across a lake to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A camel is a watertight float attached to a vessel to raise it in shallow water, a buoyancy device.

clue.text: City in Europe to fail in discussions

indicators.note: words used in spoken discussions are heard, so we want a sound-alike

parts.note: to lose is to fail

explanation.surface: A European city is going to collapse during negotiations.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, the French city's name is close to 'to lose'.
explanation.definitionFit: Toulouse is a large city in south-west France, the home of Airbus.

clue.text: Promptly give out number when recalled

indicators.note: something recalled is called back, so these letters run backwards

parts.note: to emit is to give out

explanation.surface: Someone promptly hands out a number when asked to remember it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when recalled' turns EMITNO round.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something on time means doing it at the stated hour, punctually or promptly.

clue.text: Leave all but composer

indicators.note: all but a word is the word with its final letter cut away

parts.note: Gustav Holst, composer of The Planets

explanation.surface: Abandon everything except the musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all but' drops Holst's last letter. HOLS is British informal for holidays.
explanation.definitionFit: Leave is time off from work, and hols are holidays: a synonym pairing.

clue.text: Simple organism, I note, small and terribly dull externally

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

indicators.note: something placed externally goes around the outside of the other part
terribly means in a dreadful state, a signal that these letters are muddled

parts.note: a memo is a short written note

explanation.surface: Someone writes a note about something small and very boring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' rearranges the fodder word into LULD, and 'externally' wraps that round the middle pair; 'small' is placed in front even though it comes later in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Slime moulds are primitive amoeba-like life forms once classed as fungi, a simple kind of organism.

clue.text: Developing respect without missing royal staff?

indicators.note: something developing is changing shape, so these letters form a new order

parts.note: less can mean without, as in 'less tax'

explanation.surface: A growing respect for doing without the missing royal staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A sceptre is a monarch's ceremonial rod, so lacking one is a whimsical sense of royal staff missing; hence the question mark.

clue.text: Go before stake, church adhering to vacuous doctrine

parts.note: an ante is the stake put in before a poker hand
CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: a vacuous word is empty, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A wager precedes a church sticking to an empty creed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adhering to' is a link, the empty doctrine sticks to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To antecede is to precede, coming earlier in time or order.

clue.text: Dog almost catching favourite rabbit

indicators.note: one word catching another holds it within its letters
almost means the word is cut short, losing its end

parts.note: to dog is to tail or follow
a pet is a favourite

explanation.surface: A hound nearly grabs a beloved rabbit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog' looks like a noun chasing the rabbit, but it is the verb meaning to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: The tapeti is a wild South American rabbit species, also called the Brazilian cottontail.

clue.text: Heads of army invading Turkey putting lock around betrayer

indicators.note: putting one part around another wraps it round the outside

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair

indicators.note: only the leading letter of each of the two words is taken

parts.note: TR is the international vehicle code for Turkey

explanation.surface: An army invading Turkey makes a betrayer's hair be locked in place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' has the lock enclosing the army-and-invading heads plus the Turkey code, which go in after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A traitress is a female traitor, someone who betrays.

clue.text: Indonesian stone transported around island

indicators.note: one part sitting around another encloses it
carried off and moved about, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the map abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A stone from Indonesia is shipped round an island.
explanation.walkthrough: A nesiot is an island-dweller, so an Indonesian fits as an example; 'Indonesian' looks like an adjective for 'stone'.
explanation.definitionFit: Indonesia is an archipelago nation, so an Indonesian is an example of an islander.

clue.text: Bird is something seen around island

indicators.note: a word seen around another is placed about it, enclosing it

parts.note: what can mean something, as in 'I'll tell you what'
an inch is a Scottish word for a small island

explanation.surface: A bird is something spotted near an island.
explanation.walkthrough: INCH is Scottish for a small island, as in Inchcolm.
explanation.definitionFit: The whinchat is a small brown songbird of open countryside, a chat species.

clue.text: Service vessel with line up above

indicators.note: in a down entry, one part above another comes first
in a down entry, going up means the word reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a row is a line
a ship is a vessel

explanation.surface: A church service held on a boat whose rigging rises overhead.
explanation.definitionFit: Worship is a religious service, such as morning worship in church.

clue.text: Contained protesters with strange instrument

parts.note: kettling is the police tactic of penning protesters in a confined area
rum is British informal for odd or strange

explanation.surface: Police held demonstrators who carried an odd instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' looks like an adjective for 'instrument', but it supplies RUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A kettledrum is a large bowl-shaped drum, the timpani of an orchestra, so a percussion instrument.

clue.text: Muse or Queen tattoos regularly seen

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

indicators.note: taking letters regularly means picking every other one in turn

explanation.surface: An artist's muse, or the Queen, spotted with tattoos.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is one of the nine Muses of Greek myth, the one presiding over love poetry.

clue.text: Digging by Truro on vacation

parts.note: in can mean by, as in 'in the post'

indicators.note: a word on vacation is emptied of its middle, leaving its outside letters

explanation.surface: Excavating near a Cornish city while on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: TRURO is the cathedral city of Cornwall in south-west England; vacated it leaves its outside pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Being into something is informal for enjoying it, and digging is slang for liking it.

clue.text: Times covering trendy revolutionary snack

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so the letters read backwards
a word covering another goes around it

parts.note: eras are times or ages
in means fashionable or trendy

explanation.surface: A newspaper writes up a fashionable radical's sandwich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' gives EINRAS and 'revolutionary' turns it round. SARNIE is British slang for a sandwich.
explanation.definitionFit: A sarnie is a sandwich, a typical quick snack.

clue.text: On reflection, yes, getting fine always brings complaint

indicators.note: a reflection shows a mirror image, so this word reads backwards

parts.note: yah is a posh form of yes
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
ever means always

explanation.surface: Thinking it over, agreeing to be fined for good brings complaints.
explanation.definitionFit: Hay fever is an allergic illness, and complaint can mean an ailment.

clue.text: Ultimately every little helps, of course

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the closing letter of each word is taken

explanation.surface: The supermarket slogan that every little helps, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Every little helps' is the slogan of the British supermarket Tesco.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Of course' is an emphatic agreement, the same as saying yes.

clue.text: Starts shooting in prisons, press going outside

indicators.note: one word going outside another wraps round it

parts.note: OUP is Oxford University Press
pens are enclosures, so prisons

explanation.surface: Gunfire breaks out in jails as journalists leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word here.
explanation.definitionFit: To open up is to begin firing guns, starting a burst of shooting.

clue.text: Viewing problems perhaps caused by 22 on the way

indicators.note: in an across entry one part on another follows it

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
the answer to 22 down, meaning of course

explanation.surface: Eye trouble brought on by agreement while travelling.
explanation.walkthrough: Styes are eyelid infections; 'perhaps' flags them as an example of eye trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is a painful lump on the eyelid that can blur sight, an example of eye trouble.
